Sometimes growth is easier to appreciate when you finally look back.

A few new customers here, a small increase in MRR there, and another month of steady retention might not feel remarkable on their own. Over time, those changes can add up to meaningful progress.

My Subscription Health Power BI Kit helps make that longer story visible: https://garrettsdevdesk.etsy.com/listing/4595420792/power-bi-subscription-dashboard-template

A month of modest subscription growth can feel uneventful when you're focused on the next target.

But small gains in customers and recurring revenue can become much more meaningful when you see several months together. A longer view helps you recognize progress that might be easy to overlook.

Try comparing today's MRR and active customer count with the same figures six months ago. What has changed, and which improvements deserve recognition?

Six months ago, your subscription business might have looked quite different from today.

New customers arrived, recurring revenue changed, and some plans grew faster than others. A historical view helps you see those developments together instead of remembering only the latest reporting period.

My Subscription Health Power BI Kit brings historical trends and subscription metrics into one report: https://garrettsdevdesk.etsy.com/listing/4595420792/power-bi-subscription-dashboard-template

Progress rarely looks like a perfectly smooth line on a dashboard.

Some months bring stronger growth, while others include more churn, contractions, or slower customer acquisition. Looking at the longer trend can help you understand those difficult periods without ignoring them.

Try reviewing twelve months of MRR movement. Which months stand out, and what happened afterward? The full timeline may tell a more useful story than any single result.

A dashboard can become a useful record of how far a business has come.

When you can revisit MRR, customer growth, churn, ARPU, and plan performance over time, you gain perspective on both the progress and the challenges along the way. That history can make the next decision more informed.

I designed my Subscription Health Power BI Kit with that kind of reporting in mind: https://garrettsdevdesk.etsy.com/listing/4595420792/power-bi-subscription-dashboard-template

It's easy to spend so much time looking toward the next business goal that you forget to appreciate what's already changed.

Historical reporting can help you recognize the customers gained, revenue earned, and difficult periods worked through along the way. The numbers don't tell every part of the story, but they can preserve a meaningful record of progress.

When was the last time you looked back at six or twelve months of business results and felt encouraged by what you saw?
